The candidate claimed for reverse KL: 'the divergence blows up in regions where P(x) > 0 but Q(x) tends to zero'. This is the error for the forward KL direction, not reverse.

The claim that 'Cauchy has a well-defined mean at its location parameter' is false.
The claim that 'convergence to a normal is merely very slow rather than absent' is false for the Cauchy distribution.

The candidate incorrectly claims that 'MAP has the advantage of being invariant to reparameterisation'. The MAP estimator is famously not invariant to non-linear reparameterisations because the mode of a probability density function changes under change of variables (due to the Jacobian determinant).

The candidate incorrectly claims 'the mode is a property of the distribution itself' as a justification for invariance; the mode is a property of the density, which is not invariant under transformation.
Reverse KL, D(Q||P), is zero-forcing (mode-seeking); forward KL is mass-covering.
